direct_hits.title: Systems and methods for minimally invasive drug delivery to a subarachnoid space
direct_hits.relevance: CEREVASC'S OWN PATENT — covers METHOD of endovascular drug delivery to ISAS via 3D reconstruction + fluoroscopy overlay + catheter navigation + anastomosis + therapeutic agent administration. 15 METHOD claims. Active until 2039. CONFIRMS CereVasc has already patented the basic endovascular CNS drug delivery method.
direct_hits.impact_on_T9: M2/M3/M6/M7/M8 (all drug delivery candidates) SATURATED by CereVasc's own IP. Any new drug delivery invention must be a SIGNIFICANT IMPROVEMENT beyond this patent. M10 (CSF biosensor) is NOT covered because patent is method-of-delivery, not biosensor.

direct_hits.title: Directional stent for accessing extravascular spaces
direct_hits.relevance: CEREVASC'S OWN PATENT — covers SYSTEM of tubular stent in venous sinus with internal scaffolding that deflects access catheter towards sinus wall for extravascular access. 15 SYSTEM claims. Active until 2042.
direct_hits.impact_on_T9: CereVasc has the ACCESS SYSTEM (directional stent) AND the DELIVERY METHOD (US11850390). Together these cover the basic endovascular CNS drug delivery infrastructure. T9 white space must be BEYOND these.

direct_hits.title: Skull-mounted drug and pressure sensor
direct_hits.relevance: MOST DIRECT COMPETITOR HIT for M10 (CSF biosensor). Claims skull-mounted implantable drug+pressure sensor (SOS) with: optical ventricular catheter, LED bundle for measuring optical absorption profile of CSF, photodetector, microcontroller subsystems, BLUETOOTH RADIO for wireless communication, drug delivery port, pressure+temperature sensor. Also claims CSF optical sensing chamber.
direct_hits.distinction_from_M10: Cognos is SKULL-MOUNTED (requires cranial burr hole); M10 is ENDOVASCULAR (via venous access, no burr hole). Cognos is standalone drug+sensor (no drainage); M10 is INTEGRATED with eShunt drainage function. Different patient population (Cognos: Alzheimer's/Parkinson's via burr hole; M10: NPH/IIH with venous access).
direct_hits.impact_on_M10: M10 SURVIVES but WEAKENED. Concept of wireless CSF biomarker sensing + Bluetooth + drug delivery is TAUGHT by Cognos. M10 must claim endovascular route + drainage integration + specific biosensor modality not taught by Cognos (electrochemical / microfluidic / multi-analyte array).

direct_hits.title: Apparatus and method for cerebral microdialysis to treat neurological disease, including Alzheimer's, Parkinson's or multiple sclerosis
direct_hits.inventor: Roger Kornberg, Yehoshua Shachar, Thomas Chen
direct_hits.relevance: DIRECT HIT for chronic CSF biomarker removal + drug delivery. Claims implantable catheter in brain + first pump to transport CSF + separation device (dialysis membrane impregnated with antibody / reversible electrostatic filter / magnetic field effect fractionation chamber) + second pump for drug delivery. Targets Aβ and tau protein.
direct_hits.distinction_from_M10: Cognos US11529443 is MICRODIALYSIS (continuous sampling + separation + drug delivery); M10 is BIOSENSOR (continuous measurement, no sampling). Different physical mechanism (dialysis vs sensing). Cognos is not endovascular.
direct_hits.impact_on_M10: M10 SURVIVES. Cognos US11529443 teaches CSF treatment via dialysis, not via continuous biomarker measurement. Different mechanism (separation vs sensing). But Cognos is broad patent family covering multiple CSF intervention modalities.

CONFIRMED killed by physics pre-check; preserved as honest negative per #7 M10 lesson.

M8 (chemotherapy via eShunt): SQ20 + Lens LQ19 returned DIRECT HITS — 'stop-flow programmable shunt valve' (2014) and 'programmable shunt valves with virtual off for intrathecal chemotherapy delivery' (2026). M8 is SATURATED by standard-of-care for VP shunts.

M2/M3/M6/M7 (drug delivery candidates): SATURATED by CereVasc's own US11850390B2 / EP3762083B1 (METHOD of endovascular drug delivery to ISAS). Any new drug delivery invention would need to be a SIGNIFICANT IMPROVEMENT beyond CereVasc's existing patent.

M9 (continuous ICP monitoring): Already covered by CereVasc Position 002 (dual pressure sensor patent).

M1 (drug depot in eShunt wall): SATURATED by Bactiseal (Codman) + ARES (Medtronic) antibiotic-impregnated VP shunts (SQ12: 191 Scopus hits). Plus physics pre-check confirmed eShunt drainage clears CSF-lumen drug too rapidly.

white_space_confirmed_for_M10.summary: After multi-source prior-art search (Lens COMPLETE + Scopus COMPLETE + Google Patents COMPLETE × 2 + PatSnap BLOCKED), the WHITE SPACE for T9 is confirmed as: WIRELESS BIOCHEMICAL BIOSENSOR INTEGRATED INTO ENDOVASCULAR CSF SHUNT for chronic multi-analyte CSF biomarker monitoring.
evidence_for_white_space: CereVasc's own US11850390B2 / EP3762083B1 covers METHOD of DRUG DELIVERY to ISAS, not BIOSENSOR. CereVasc's US11883309B2 covers directional stent ACCESS SYSTEM, not biosensor.
Cognos US10786155B2 covers skull-mounted drug+pressure+optical sensor (skull-mounted, not endovascular).
Cognos US11529443B2 covers cerebral microdialysis (separation device, not continuous biosensor).
Cognos US20230191095A1 covers inline pressure+temperature sensor on cerebral shunt (mechanical, not biochemical).
Multiple VP shunt mechanical sensors exist (flow, occlusion, pressure) but NONE are biochemical biosensors.
Multiple research-stage CSF biosensors exist (lab-on-chip, microfluidic, optical fiber) but NONE are integrated into endovascular shunt.
Dexcom CGM (continuous glucose monitor) establishes precedent for chronic implantable biosensor; CSF analog is novel.
evidence_against_white_space: Cognos has a patent FAMILY (US10786155B2, US11529443B2, US11883203B2, US20230191095A1) covering multiple aspects of CSF drug+sensor integration. §103 obviousness risk: PHOSITA could adapt Cognos skull-mounted design to endovascular route.
Intellectual Ventures (Invention Science Fund) broad patents on infection-fighting implantable devices create §103 risk.
Medtronic US6248080B1 (2001) covers intracranial monitoring + therapy delivery — broad conceptual prior art.
Research-stage CSF biosensors (optical fiber, microfluidic) establish that the technical components exist; integration into endovascular shunt could be argued as obvious combination.
M10_must_claim: INTEGRATED with CSF drainage function (not standalone sensor)
WIRELESS multi-analyte BIOCHEMICAL biosensor (not mechanical pressure/flow/occlusion sensor)
Flow-past-sensor architecture (CSF drainage flow continuously refreshes analyte at sensor surface — unique to eShunt vs static Ommaya sampling)
eShunt patient population (NPH/IIH with existing venous access)
